name: God, Christ & the Holy Ghost
about: The one true God, the deity of Christ, and the Comforter.

teachings.title: In the beginning was the Word
teachings.summary: John opens by establishing that Jesus is the eternal Word, God and with God, the Creator, refuting modalism and claims that Jesus is not God.
teachings.text:
John hits the ground running. No human genealogies. Not the human birth of Christ, but the divine godhead of Jesus.

The Word is God's promise. The Word is the written testimony of God to man. The Word is who made all things and gave life, to creation and man. He was the light. He is God, and always was.

John begins his testimonial of the good news letting the reader know beyond a shadow of a doubt that Jesus is God, and was with God in the beginning.

**Genesis 1**
*26 And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.*

John establishes first that Jesus always was. Always was God and always was with God, the Father. It's the first doctrine of the Gospel. You have to accept that there is a God, that His Word is true. That Jesus is fully of the godhead, and eternal, and God is the creator of all things and the spark of life for that creation.

5 verses that dispels modalism, oneness heresy. Dispels the "Jesus didn't exist until he was born" heresy. The "Jesus isn't God" heresy. 5 verses that lay a foundation for the faith.

teachings.title: The I am sayings of Jesus
teachings.summary: Jesus' seven I am sayings in John, and before Abraham was, I am, declare His divinity and that eternal life comes only through Him.
teachings.text:
In the Gospel of John, Jesus is quoted 7 times* making affirmation of who He is, using the divine "*I am*," (as God the Father said to Moses from the burning bush). This formulation would be a sign to some, recognizing Jesus was Christ and a stumbling block to the hypocrites who challenged Jesus at every turn, leading eventually to His arrest and crucifixion.

They are:

1) John 6:48 *I am that bread of life.*

2) John 8:12 *Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.*

3) John 10:9 *I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture*.

4) John 10:11 *I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.*

5) John 11:25 *Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:*

6) John 14:6 *Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.*

7) John 15:1 *I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.*

From these we see Jesus' nature as the source of eternal life and our salvation through Him. His sacrifice and His love.

*There is an 8th instance, in John 8:57 *Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I am.***”** - which serves as an emphatic statement on the Son's divinity, and timeless origin. Jesus always has been. He is who am. And as always, the Jews reaction to the truth was anger and violence; "*So they picked up stones to throw at him*."

teachings.title: The Son honoured as the Father
teachings.summary: Jesus teaches His authority comes from the Father, that the Godhead are three persons yet one, and that whoever hears and believes hath everlasting life and shall not come into condemnation.
teachings.text:
The remaining verses of the chapter are all red letter preaching by Jesus.

Jesus establishes His sonship with the Father. That He emulates and gets His authority from the Father. That His dominion as the Son is the authority of the Father, and to honor the Father you must honor Jesus.

This is pure doctrine.

Next Jesus again gives the good news of the Gospel; Saying He is telling us truthfully that any who hear God's word, His testimony of Christ, and believe, **has** everlasting life and **shall not** come I to condemnation. (Again showing that once we are saved it is forever. We HAVE everlasting life. We WON'T be condemned)

Jesus preaches that the dead in spirit will hear His voice, His word, and live. Salvation quickens, or makes alive, our dead spirit inside and brings us into life.

Jesus says not to marvel at the basic Gospel, just wait until the resurrection of the dead!

Jesus again teaches He is not there for His own will, but that of the Father. Each member of the Godhead has His own will, are their own person, Father, the Son and the Spirit. But these three are one and obey the will of God the Father.

Jesus accuses the Jews of not believing the witness of those testifying He is Christ and what He says is true. He points to John the Baptist as one, then the Holy Ghost, the works of God the Father Jesus does, and the very scriptures that the Pharisees claim their authority from, that testifies to who Jesus is.

The Jews claim to believe in the resurrection of the dead and the salvation of the Christ, but they don't have the truth in them, and so they can't see it when He's literally in front of them.

teachings.title: Christ the image of the invisible God
teachings.summary: Jesus is the express image of the Father, creator of all and firstborn from the dead, who reconciles believers to God, and being translated into His kingdom is a change of spirit, not of body.
teachings.text:
Here in the opening of Paul's letter to the saints at Colosse, we have one of the most eloquent descriptions of who Jesus is and our shared faith in Him.

Note again, Paul prays for God's grace, and the peace that comes from it for those reading. It is only possible to have peace by having peace with God, and that peace is only possible by being partakers of His grace. And all knowledge and wisdom of God's word comes from Him, and those sincerely seeking it. Paul wishes all this that the Colossians may continue being fruitful, sharing the faith and winning more to the body of the church, which is Christ's. Preached to every creature.

Strengthened with His glorious power, that we may endure all things with longsuffering and patience and joy. Delivered with His blood. Redeemed by Him. Partakers of the inheritance of the light, saved from the darkness. Translated into the Kingdom of Heaven.

(This is the biblical meaning of being translated in regards to our spiritual state, and the Kingdom. It is not the bodily assumption of our corruptible flesh, as some presume, but a change of our spirit, quickened by the Holy Ghost, made acceptable by the blood)

Jesus is the express image of God the Father, and made through Jesus, all that has been created is His, who was before all things. Who is the first fruits of the resurrection, so that He may have preeminence in even that, making peace with God through the cross, reconciling all things.

And for us who are grounded and settled to this Gospel of reconciliation:

*And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled. In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight.*

We who were dead in sin, enemies of God through our wicked works, made unblameable and unreproveable before God, reconciled with the Father by the Son. Our sins forever forgiven.

And Paul made a minister unto the Gentiles, suffering in the flesh for the Gospel's sake, to edify, build up, the body which is the congregation of believers, serving the head which is Christ Jesus. Rejoicing in this suffering, Paul encourages us with this joy, that we may preach to every man and win every man to the same peace we have through grace in Christ.

teachings.title: David's Lord at the right hand of God
teachings.summary: From Psalm 110 Jesus shows the Christ is not merely David's son but David's Lord, seated at God's right hand, and the vain scribes earn greater condemnation.
teachings.text:
Jesus having exposed the errors of the hypocrite Pharisees and Sadducees now took aim at the scribes asking how say they that the Christ is the son of David, quoting **Psalm 110**:

*The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.*

*2 The LORD shall send the rod of thy strength out of Zion: rule thou in the midst of thine enemies.*

*3 Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power, in the beauties of holiness from the womb of the morning: thou hast the dew of thy youth.*

*4 The LORD hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.*

*5 The Lord at thy right hand shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath.*

*6 He shall judge among the heathen, he shall fill the places with the dead bodies; he shall wound the heads over many countries.*

Jesus asks how can a physical son be called Lord by David, himself a king at the writing of the Psalm. And Jesus notes the indication of God the Father, LORD, proclaiming the Adonai, the Lord, Christ, the anointed, the Messiah, is so much more than an earthly king, or a son of David.

The crowd who welcomed Him with palms and praise just days before all recognized Jesus as the son of David, promised by God through the prophets, but here Jesus makes clear what exactly that means. That He is the Christ that is seated at the right hand of God, and the people who he was teaching to received this teaching gladly.

Then, turning to rebuke the scribes who should know better than the people, who should have been those to proclaim the truth, being keepers of the law, Jesus exposes what their actual priorities are; being seen, being honored, being special boys given praise, preferential treatment and working their way in to widows houses to drain them of their wealth with their false teachings and spirituality without the Spirit.

Many such cases today, both in Christianity and in secular spiritual nonsense. Giving long public prayers to show how righteous they are. Wearing long robes to denote their high station, sitting in the choice seats of the synagogue as lords over the common people, using the word of God as their own wealth and prestige, like the parable of the unjust steward from **Luke 16**.

And they earn themselves a greater condemnation, being given worse punishment in Hell for their transgression.

teachings.title: The Names of Christ in Revelation
teachings.summary: Revelation gives many names of Christ, including the Word of God, as He rides out after the marriage supper to the short battle of Armageddon.
teachings.text:
Alleluia! God be praised! The only appearance of the term, also spelled as hallelujah, (note Jah), transliterated from the Hebrew, but given us in Greek here, He is worthy of praise indeed.

Chapter 19 gives more detail to the triumphant beginning of the Kingdom of Heaven, Jesus Christ the Lord taking over the kingdoms of this earth, which we glimpsed in chapter 11;

*And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.*

*And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, We give thee thanks, O Lord God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.*

Chapter 19 opens with a clear indication of the order of things we have read and John witnessed. Another "after these things," that we may know with certain faith that this is following the wrath, the same wrath as the trumpets and the same as the vials.

And again the inspired revelation gives us more names of Jesus, that we may worship Him, and in doing so makes us better understand the scriptures that precede **Revelation**.

I cribbed this list to put them in order and perspective:

1. Jesus Christ (Revelation1:1).
2. Faithful Witness (Revelation 1:5).
3. First Begotten Of The Dead (Revelation 1:5).
4. Prince Of The Kings Of The Earth (Revelation 1:5).
5. Alpha And Omega (Revelation 1:8-13).
6. First And Last (Revelation 1:8, 11, 13).
7. Son Of Man (Revelation 1;13).
8. He That Liveth And Was Dead (Revelation 1:13, 18).
9. He That Holdeth The Seven Stars (Revelation 2:1).
10. He Who Walketh Midst The Golden Candlesticks (Revelation 2:1).
11. He Who Hath The Sharp Sword With Two Edges (Revelation 2:12).
12. Son Of God (Revelation 2:18).
13. He Which Searches The Reins And Hearts (Revelation 2:23).
14. He That Hath The Seven Spirits Of God (Revelation 3:1).
15. He That Hath The Seven Stars (Revelation 3:1).
16. He That Is Holy And True (Revelation 3:7).
17. He That Hath The Key Of David (Revelation 3:7).
18. He That Openeth And No Man Shutteth (Revelation 3:7).
19. He That Shutteth And No Man Openeth (Revelation 3:7).
20. The Amen (Revelation 3:14).
21. The Faithful And True Witness (Revelation 3:14).
22. The Beginning Of The Creation Of God (Revelation 3:14).
23. Lord (Revelation 4:11).
24. Lion Of The Tribe Of Judah (Revelation 5:5,9).
25. The Root Of David (Revelation 5:5,9)
26. A Lamb As It Had Been Slain (Revelation 5:6-7).
27. The Lamb (Revelation 5:8-9).
28. Lord Of Lords (Revelation 17:14).
29. King Of Kings (Revelation 17:14).
30. Faithful And True (Revelation 19:11).
31. Rider Of The White Horse (Revelation 19:11).
32. The Word Of God (Revelation 19:13).
33. Christ (Revelation 20:4).
34. The Lord God Of The Holy Prophets (Revelation 22:6).
35. Beginning And The End (Revelation 22:13).
36. The Bright And Morning Star (Revelation 22:16).

Amen. And in chapter 19 we see further Jesus will come *with a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.*

The only time in the King James Bible that the Word of God is capitalized, making it a Name of Christ who is the Word made flesh. Faithful and true.

And the multitudes in Heaven, the saints called to the marriage supper, given wedding garments, white, the fine linen is the righteousness of saints. And a saint in heaven, a man redeemed in Christ, tells John to write;

*Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of God.*

The wedding feast of **Matthew 22** is come. Alleluia.

And the Lord rides out on a white horse, followed by the army of the saints upon their own, as the beast and his prophet and the armies of those who worshipped the beast ride out to do battle against Him;

**Revelation 16:16**
*And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon*

This is the battle of Armageddon. It is short lived.

teachings.title: Made a Little Lower Than the Angels
teachings.summary: Christ the Creator was made flesh and tasted death for every man, freeing believers from the devil's power of death and the fear of it.
teachings.text:
Having established Jesus as Christ, the redeemer, higher than the angels, Creator and the Son of God, our salvation to whom all the prophets gave witness, Paul builds upon this truth with the implications of our faith.

Since Jesus is, therefore we should give greater heed, pay closer attention to the things spoken of by God, in diverse manners by the prophets to the fathers and by Lord Jesus Himself. That every transgression of the law (for sin is the transgression of the law) shall receive a "just recompense." Death and Hell. Just as the angels who rebelled will be all brought in subjection and cast into that lake of fire promised in Revelation, so too will man be if they neglect the good news of salvation, spoken of by the Lord and confirmed by those who witnessed Jesus ministry, and by signs and wonders of God, and through the gifts of the Holy Ghost given the disciples and Apostles.

He's saying, "Look, we know who Jesus is not only by reputation but by scripture, the prophets, His followers who got it directly from Him, and we know about the fate of those angels who rebelled, Whom Jesus is greater than as He has them under subjection, so we need to listen and believe."

But Jesus was also a man. Citing scripture, Paul notes how God made Jesus a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, that He may taste death for all men. That the Creator became as the created that he may bring us to glory. That He, as the captain of our salvation was made perfect, complete, by the suffering of the cross and death as a sin offering.

For in Christ, we believers are His brethren, His brothers. Sanctified in Jesus we become as one with Him, sons adopted into the promise of His glory by the Father. Who Jesus is not ashamed to call brethren.

Again and again, citing scripture that his audience would know, primarily the Psalms of David which teach so much doctrine, he lays out the case for his argument. By taking heed we are the children of God by the partaking of Jesus flesh and blood through His death. And by His resurrection, steal the power of death from the devil.

Satan was a murderer from the beginning. His goal is to ensure every man faces death and Hell like him. To sin, and in sin, be condemned. This is the power of death the devil possesses.

But Christ's triumph granting salvation to all who believe, and eternal life to never taste death, delivered us. Set free from the bondage of the law, which by fear of death we try and fail to save ourselves. But in Christ, liberated from that fear knowing we won't die for our sins, as they are forgiven in Him.

And so, to provide this salvation Jesus took on the form of man. And in all things He was like us, tempted of the flesh that He may know our struggles and understand our pain, that He may serve as the propitiation for our sin and succour, comfort us, in our temptations and afflictions.

This is so important to understand.

That God so loved us, that He so regarded man, that He allowed the express image of His person, His only begotten Son, through Whom all things were made and under Whom all things will be brought under subjection, to be made lower than the angels, to be made flesh and blood, to be tempted and suffer and made sin for all, that we may have eternal life. Liberated from the fear of death found in transgression of the law by our redemption in His perfect work. Just as the prophets and scriptures promised. Just as those who came before believed on for salvation.

This is the good news. This is the Gospel.

teachings.title: Jesus grew in wisdom as a man
teachings.summary: Fully God yet fully man, Jesus grew in spirit and wisdom and had to learn the scriptures as we do, an example of hearing and committing God's word to heart.
teachings.text:
Jesus, being fully man and fully God, was born as we are. He grew as we do. He waxed in spirit and filled with wisdom, meaning He grew into these things.

When we see the story of a young Jesus who tarries behind in the temple after going with His family to celebrate the feast of Passover, it is often portrayed as Jesus instructing the scribes there. But the Bible tells us that Jesus was seeking knowledge and understanding from them.

Yes He was fully God, but in the flesh, He was tempted, tested, in all things as we are, being fully man as well.

He waxed in spirit. He filled in wisdom. He grew physically and in knowledge.

*And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions. And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers.*

He astonished them with His ability to understand, but He sought to gain wisdom and knowledge. He was about His Father's business.

Some believe he came out of the womb with the full knowledge of everything, and had the whole word of God memorized in His heart, being the author of it. But this story found only in Luke paints a picture of a child who had to grow into a man as we do. And while He was perfect in His ways and without sin, that didn't mean He didn't hunger, thirst or have to devote Himself to learn scripture, just as we do. Jesus' did the will of His Father as an example to us. And God calls upon us to hear His word, question the meaning, learn His statutes, and commit His word to our hearts. Things that take discipline and faith, of which Jesus was the ultimate example.

And again, Mary took these things and remembered them, trying to understand just what it meant, that Jesus was Christ.

*For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.*

teachings.title: Jesus chose the Father's will at every step
teachings.summary: As a man Jesus chose at every moment to do the Father's will rather than yield to the flesh, so that He could call us to do the same in His grace.
teachings.text:
The implications of this are important to consider. That Jesus as man had to, at every step of His life, choose to do the will of the Father, putting that above His own will and the weaknesses of the flesh He resided in.

Jesus had to choose to be without sin, though He suffered in the flesh. He chose to learn the word of God as a man would. Devote His time and energy to pleasing His heavenly Father and honoring His earthly parents. Not letting discomfort, cold, hunger, thirst, frustrations, humiliation, or any other thing being Him to sin. Yes the grace of God was upon Him. But we who are saved have a similar grace, but still sin.

He grew, He waxed in the Spirit. He grew in knowledge and wisdom, one day at a time, choosing at every opportunity to do the will of Him Who sent Him, so that He could call us to do the same. In that grace. In that love. Amen.

teachings.title: Jesus felt the weight of time
teachings.summary: The eternal Son, existing outside time, took on flesh bound by time, and that constraint was part of what He suffered as our Saviour.
teachings.text:
Reading **Luke 9:46-62**, closing out the chapter, it seems like a litany of man trying Jesus patience, and His trying to impress certain lessons and understanding, His time growing short.

Time is of the essence of what makes man, man. And Jesus, being fully God and fully man had to feel the weight of it more acutely than anyone who ever lived.

As God, the Alpha and Omega, there from the beginning and through the end, the Godhead exists outside time, being trapped within it must have been trying, the infirmities of man constraining Him. Part of what Jesus suffered to be our savior. As much a part of His sacrifice as the cross.

Time is a construct, a part of creation, the means by which life and death, creation and corruption are expressed. And Jesus being incorruptible, made a little lower than the angels, putting on corruptible flesh that we may be saved.

And with full knowledge and understanding of the Father's will, and with time growing short, Jesus tried His best to give His followers and those who wished to be, the reality of what it would mean, who He was, what the Christ must suffer, and yet they understand not.

*O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you, and suffer you?*

teachings.title: Today shalt thou be with me in paradise
teachings.summary: The thief on the cross shows salvation by faith alone, and Christ's promise of paradise shows He is God in heaven, not that He skipped Hell for a waiting room.
teachings.text:
We see the story of the thief on the cross, told again in Luke. The one mocking Jesus, the other recognizing His being Christ, calls upon His name, saying *Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.*

*And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, Today shalt thou be with me in paradise.*

This is a beautiful example of salvation by faith, that even heretical cults that teach a salvation of works admit is an example of justification by faith alone. They claim it is an exemption, but it is the only way to salvation, offered to us as an example that there can be no doubt.

Others use the saying of Jesus to indicate that Jesus didn't die and go to Hell for 3 days and nights, but instead went to some waiting room in Hell called "paradise." This is contrary to scripture and to the very act with which we believe on for salvation. Jesus died for us. Jesus became sin for us. Death and Hell are the punishment for sin, and Jesus was the burnt offering, the substitution for ourselves, God's only begotten Son. Jehovahjireh.

What then?

Simply that Jesus is also God.

**John 3:11-13**
*Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things? And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven.*

The Son of man which **is** in heaven, is the same as the man Christ Jesus sitting before Nicodemus at that moment.

Jesus being fully God was also fully man. He was made flesh and dwelt among us. But He was always with God and was God.

*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.*

And so there is no great contradiction or doubtful disputation found in this verse. Paradise is Heaven and God is the God of the living. In death, is Hell.

*And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.*

teachings.title: Jesus is the promised Shepherd
teachings.summary: When Jesus says I am the Good Shepherd He declares He is the Lord of Ezekiel 34, whose flock is believers, not Jews after the flesh.
teachings.text:
Jesus is the promised Shepherd.

He maketh us lie down in green pastures. He searches out for the lost. He heals us he feeds us and watches over us from our enemies.

He judges the other cattle for their treatment of his sheep and the pasture that he had given them and the waters he had provided them.

Notice here in Ezekiel 34, which begins the hopeful prophecies of Salvation in the last part of the book, that the Lord says *Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out*.

He uses this assurance a few times. When Jesus says *I am the Good Shepherd*, He is directly stating that he is the Lord.

Further down, we see *even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.* Just as Jesus is the Son of God, He is a son of David.

And there are sheep of other folds that he brings in and makes us one fold. This is the promise. It is not to Jews after the flesh. It is not to a physical nation of Israel. Although certainly the fold has sheep from among them.

But the bad shepherds are the religious leaders, false prophets and wayward priests of Israel. And further the Lord says he will judge His flock, and cattle with cattle, these are the physical Jews, after the flesh. He's clearly delineating between believers and unbelievers. Between His sheep who hear His voice and those that trample down the fields and pollute the waters.

The promise of eternal peace, safety and security, freedom from attack of enemies without and corruption from within, is all given to His flock.

*The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.* Amen

teachings.title: Jesus is the excellent name of the Lord
teachings.summary: Psalm 8 praises Christ, who is God, the Creator through whom all things were made, the I AM given the name above every name, and the only name under heaven by which men must be saved and worshipped.
teachings.text:
The excellent name of our Lord is Jesus.

**Psalm 8** is a song of praise for the Christ. The name of the Lord, who has been set by the LORD, God the Father, over all things. Who also is God.

Jesus is the anointed, Who is ordained to strength, and mighty.

**Hebrews 2:4–9**
*God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will? For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak. But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him. But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.*

The New Testament reveals the intent and interpretation of the Old. We see Jesus using Psalm 8:2 against the Pharisees, showing that He is the name of God;

**Matthew 21:15–17**
*And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were sore displeased, And said unto him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise? And he left them, and went out of the city into Bethany; and he lodged there*.

Through His name was all creation made:

**Colossians 1:16–17**
*For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.*

**John 1:1–3**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.*

*The same was in the beginning*, when men first called upon the name of the Lord.

**Genesis 4:25–26**
*And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.*

Jesus has been made to have dominion over all things, that the glory and honor be given to Him.

**Ephesians 1:9–10**
*Having made known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him*

And the excellency of His name is revealed in Christ Jesus.

**Philippians 2:9–11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.*

Jesus is the name of the Lord. Of the great I Am.

**John 8:56–58**
*Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad. Then said the Jews unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham? Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.*

No other name is given by God to be worshipped as God.

**Acts 4:12**
*Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.*

teachings.title: Thou art the Christ
teachings.summary: The title Christ was a loaded term for the anointed deliverer the Jews expected, and believing that Jesus is the Christ is what is required to be born of God.
teachings.text:
This is why, so frequently in the Gospels and Epistles, Christ is used as a kind of shorthand that carries all of this meaning in the context of Jesus being that Anointed One.

**John 1:40–42**
*One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother. He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ. And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone.*

Andrew heard from John the Baptist, that Jesus was the Messias, the Christ, and immediately knew what that meant. He tells Simon Peter, who understands the implications.

The term "Christ" was a heavily loaded, shorthand title that required no basic definition for a 1st-century, faithful, Jewish audience.

The concept of a coming, anointed deliverer was deeply woven into the fabric of the Jews' expectation, rooted in Old Testament prophecies of a King from the line of David, a Priest, or a Prophet, to deliver them.

In **Matthew 16:16**, Peter delivers his landmark declaration: *Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.*

During Jesus' trial, the high priest asks him point-blank:

**Mark 14:60–61**
*And the high priest stood up in the midst, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee? But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and said unto him, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?*

The religious leaders had an understanding of the scriptural definition of the Christ; they just believed Jesus was blasphemously claiming it.

But it is His to claim. And faith in this truth is what is required of man to be saved. The shorthand of the Christ, that carries so much spiritual weight.

**1 John 5:1**
*Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him*.

And His anointing of joy is then given to we who believe, that our joy always be full.

**1 John 1:3–4**
*That which we have seen and heard declare we unto you, that ye also may have fellowship with us: and truly our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ. And these things write we unto you, that your joy may be full*.

teachings.title: The Comforter shall teach you all things
teachings.summary: The Holy Ghost, the third person of the Trinity, dwells in believers to teach them, bring scripture to remembrance and give peace without fear.
teachings.text:
Jesus tells them the nature of the 3rd person of the trinity, the Holy Ghost. The Comforter. Who, dwelling within us gives us discernment to understand the word, as He teaches us all things and brings to remembrances those doctrines and scripture we've been taught.

In Him is peace, to not be troubled or afraid. The disciples would have much to fear in the coming days, and Jesus is assuring them. Our troubles are little in comparison. Why be afraid? Do you not have the Comforter? The disciples wouldn't until Pentecost! Just the words of Jesus and faith in His promise.

He tells them to rejoice in these coming days, because of that faith in that promise, and the power and faithfulness of God the Father.

With that He says His final goodbye, that He won't get to speak to them much again as the goes willingly to His fate. The prince of this world coming for Him. But Jesus is resigned to do His Father's will, and finishes with that resignation; "*Arise, let us go hence."*

teachings.title: Pentecost tongues were real languages
teachings.summary: The Holy Ghost first indwelt believers when Christ breathed on them in John 20, and at Pentecost He filled them to preach the gospel in real foreign languages, not charismatic gibberish.
teachings.text:
Acts chapter 2 picks up now, 10 days after Jesus' ascension, the 120 disciples and Apostles gathered in church, waiting in Jerusalem as Jesus had instructed. As they waited, suddenly the great room they were in was filled with a rushing wind and flames of fire, filling those assembled with the Holy Ghost.

The traditional teaching of this chapter says that this is the first time the Holy Ghost is indwelling in believers, quickening their spirit the same way saved Christians experience today, calling upon the name of the Lord. It's often preached as "until Pentecost, no one had the indwelling of the Holy Ghost." The Bible says in the OT believers who called upon the name of the Lord and were saved by faith did not have the Holy Ghost permanently within them, but were often described as being filled with Him at times to do great feats, prophesy and preach, or be used in some way to the glory of God. I believe this is what's happening here, because in John 20:22 (which we just [read](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/2295)), where risen Christ appears to them on Easter Sunday, the scripture says:

*And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost.*

I believe this was when the Holy Ghost, the comforter and 3rd person of the triune Godhead, first indwelled in those who are quickened by faith, in God's grace.

I could be wrong but that's how it reads to me, otherwise John is contradicting Acts, impossible. Given the context of what happens next, I think my interpretation is correct.

Now, on the primary holy day of the feast of [Pentecost,](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/2367) believing, practicing Jews from all over the world were required to make pilgrimage to Jerusalem and the temple for the feast of first fruits of the harvest, and the blood free will sacrifices of purification (Exodus 23:16, 34:22, Leviticus 23:16, Numbers 28:26).

The Bible says that these Jews came from every nation, and lists many of the nations in example. And as the 120, filled with the Spirit come out to the crowd this gathered, they begin to preach the Gospel to all, in their own languages. This miracle of God is astounding, as these faithful God-fearing people hear the good news of Jesus Christ in their native tongue.

Not the satanic jibberish of the Charismatics and so-called Pentecostals, but clear understandable language of those assembled there.

Not the mistaken doctrine that the disciples spoke Hebrew or Aramaic or Greek, and those assembled heard it in their own languages, but if speaking to a Mede or Libyan or whatever land the pilgrims were from, they were able to communicate the Gospel to them. How do we know this? By the reaction of the Jews from Jerusalem, who mocked what they heard as unintelligible chatter as their being drunken.

This is when Peter gives a blistering sermon addressed specifically to those mocking, and an indictment of the Jews of Judea.

Peter says obviously they aren't drunken, being only 9 in the morning, but that it's fulfilled prophecy. He then quotes Joel regarding how in the last days the sons and daughters will prophesy, and uses that verse to then lead them the further prophecy of Joel of the second coming of Christ.

Peter is not simply defending their speaking in tongues, but like Jesus did repeatedly in His ministry, Peter is using scripture they should be familiar with to bring them the Gospel. He quotes Joel 3's warning of what the day of the Lord will look like, and indicating to the crowd that it is all coming true. Warning them that if they are seeing sons and daughters with signs and wonders, preaching the word, maybe they should take heed of what the rest of scripture says. That "*Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved."*

This is the Gospel.

He continues, making clear precisely who Jesus is, what He did, that He did it among them as they well know, and that despite their knowledge they killed Christ. Peter lays the blame for this squarely on the Jews in Jerusalem.

teachings.title: The ten virgins and the oil of the Spirit
teachings.summary: The oil is the Holy Spirit and the foolish virgins are professing Christians who never received Him, and none can borrow another's oil once the bridegroom comes.
teachings.text:
Matthew 25 continues the Olivette Discourse between Jesus and His disciples, where in the previous chapter He had laid out much of end times prophecy, and His warning and instruction to be watchful and mindful, like a good servant keeping the house while the Lord was away, so as to not be taken unawares at His return. And so, by way of parable, Jesus expounds on this doctrine.

The first, the parable of the 10 virgins, 5 wise, 5 foolish, awaiting the bridegroom, with their lamps. The 5 wise have lamps filled with oil, the 5 fools never bothered, and caught unawares are shut out of the marriage. And in their pleading the Lord says, "Verily I say unto you, I know you not."

The oil is the Holy Spirit, the lamps, our hearts. The foolish virgins, the unsaved who, knowing full well of the bridegroom's pending return were lazy, slumbering.

At His return, the foolish virgins beg the wise for some of their oil, for shared righteousness, but it is not the wise's to give or share. Each must get their own from Christ. And so, the foolish were locked out in the darkness, wailing.

There are many calling themselves Christian who never received the oil, never accepted the Spirit, and tarried and slept while the master is away. Like the virgins, they may well have lived chaste lives, turning from sin, present in the chambers, but never coming to the truth and repentance to be saved.

They believed they could purchase the oil, and return. Be given another chance. But once the wedding feast starts, it's too late.

teachings.title: The Spirit maketh intercession for us
teachings.summary: While we groan awaiting redemption, the indwelling Spirit helps our infirmities and intercedes for us according to the will of God.
teachings.text:
*For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?*
*But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.*

All of creation travailing in pain, as the pangs of birth, waiting for the day of our redemption. Not only they, but ourselves also.

There is a day to come where we will be redeemed and the Bible says that all of creation is like a woman giving birth, a new thing to be born, and that we ourselves are also in travail, having the firstfruits of the Spirit within us, that earnest expectation, sealed with that promise unto that day of redemption. This is our hope.

Hope is an earnest expectation of what is yet to come. It is the object of our faith. It isn't seen. It isn't present, it is what is to come. Having that deposit, we know we will be purchased. But we groan in ourselves waiting for that day. Stuck in the flesh.

But the Comforter, that is the Spirit of God as He resides within us, He does the will of God and works.

*Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.*

The Spirit, if we let Him, works on our infirmities, helps us with removing the thorns in our hearts that otherwise lead us to sin. He heals us as we walk in the Spirit.

But more, the Spirit is an intercessor, bringing our needs before the Father, even that which we don't know we have, that His will be done through us.

Thus we are conformed to His will, and in all things that glorify God and shape us as worthy vessels, as we walk in the Spirit and feed that new man inside.

teachings.title: The work of the Holy Ghost
teachings.summary: The Holy Ghost quickens, indwells, comforts and seals believers unto redemption, bears witness that they are God's children, reproves the world, teaches the word and makes intercession.
teachings.text:
The Spirit of God, the Holy Ghost, which was foretold by the prophets who were moved by Him to receive the word of God, inspired, and promised of Christ Jesus to us, the Comforter. That He may dwell within us, the Father and the Son, in the Spirit. Who quickens our dead spirit, our stoney heart, and makes us live again. Who comforts us in tribulations. Who seals us as His own, the earnest of our inheritance in Christ;

**Ephesians 4:30**
*And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.*

**Ephesians 1:13-14**
*In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

This is the promise, that we who are saved may know we are His, and that we know we have eternal life, adopted as joint-heirs, made sons of God;

**Romans 8:16**
*The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God*.

We who the Spirit indwells are given the power to free those we share the truth with from their sins, to be born again of the Spirit as we were. Through the Gospel, which is given by the Spirit of Truth, that by hearing the inspired word of God, they may believe, and by faith be saved, that they may save others in His name, by that same Spirit. Or, if they have not the Spirit of truth, to be condemned, opposing themselves. Anathema.

All men are called by the Spirit, God the Father having lifted up the Son, because the Spirit of the Comforter works to reproved the world of sin, righteousness and judgment. That they may know they need salvation, and believe.

And all knowledge is given by the Holy Ghost, who teaches us all things, making God's word understandable, as we hear His voice and follow Him. And bringing all things to remembrance, that we may be able to give a ready answer for the hope we have in Him.

And by making our prayers effectual, even as we in our sin don't know what we need, the Spirit makes intercession for us before God in Christ's name.

teachings.title: The things of God are spiritually discerned
teachings.summary: Understanding of the things of God is a gift of the Spirit through the word, so the natural man who seeks worldly wisdom finds them foolishness.
teachings.text:
Continuing this study on Spiritual Gifts, here in **1 Corinthians 2**. Paul is writing to the church at Corinth to address divisions there, the first being those disputing about who is better among them by the minister of the gospel they'd received it by.

Paul, who along with Apollos and Peter, is being touted by some as greater, and so he humbly seeks to set the record straight. That he didn't preach to them with excellency of words and speech, an orator, or with particular wisdom and logic, as the Greeks taught in their vain philosophy. He declared the testimony of God win meekness and in fear, and in much trembling. Bringing to them the knowledge of Christ crucified, a demonstration to them of the Spirit, and the power of God.

The wisdom of the world is brought to nothing by the wisdom of God. But that wisdom is only revealed, can only be known, by His Spirit.

This is a gift of the Spirit, that all are called and those that believe bear witness to the power of God and by the understanding of His word through the Holy Ghost.

The things of God are unknown to man, but by the Spirit of God.

*Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God*.

This is important. Without first believing the Gospel, preached by the power of the word of God, and the understanding by the Spirit, the things of God are foolishness to man.

The Holy Ghost teaches, not the wisdom of men, not of the world, but the spiritual things of God. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

*But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.*

The knowledge and understanding of the things of God is a gift of the Holy Ghost. The Spirit of God gives us understanding, from His word.

This is why so many who deny the simple Gospel, and chase after the wisdom of men, who seek knowledge of the world rather than the spiritual things of God, say such foolish things regarding God, salvation, doctrine and scripture. They cannot understand because these things are spiritually discerned. They are given us of the Spirit through the word.

teachings.title: Spiritual blindness and willingness to receive
teachings.summary: Heretics who seek validation rather than truth are spiritually blind, while saved people misled can be corrected by scripture if willing.
teachings.text:
This gift of the Spirit, understanding of the things of God. Even the deep things, the meat of the word, comes from studying scripture, to be approved by God. As we seek, so to He gives wisdom and understanding freely, through the Spirit within us.

We often run into people, especially now online, who are lost in heresy. Who have, what seems to us, foolish understanding of basic doctrines, that we try to correct from clear scripture, and they cannot see it.  They are spiritually blind. They trust the wisdom of other men and their own logic, given of the world, to try and figure out what are the spiritual things of God. Because they don't seek the truth, but validation for their own ideas, they cannot receive that gift of understanding the Spirit provides.

This can even strike the saved, misled by itching ears to hear false doctrine given by theologians and tradition, and every other thing but comparing spiritual things to spiritual. They may be led to understanding by being reproached with scripture. They aren't completely blind. But they still have to be willing to receive it.

Paul, inspired by the Spirit and preaching the word of God by letter, to be read to the Corinthians, is doing exactly this; Showing those willing to be given understanding, the wisdom of God.

*For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? but we have the mind of Christ*.

teachings.title: The widow's oil that never ran out
teachings.summary: The widow's oil pictures the Holy Spirit, which pays the debt of sin and fills others without running out, the best inheritance a man can leave his family.
teachings.text:
Reading this chapter, it should stand out how similar in form and content it is to how the Gospels are written. The anointed one of God going forth and having average people come to him seeking something, and miraculously receiving it by faith.

Parallels with Christ are there; Elijah as John the Baptist, a voice in the wilderness, Elisha as he who came after him, with twice the spirit of the Lord upon him. The sons of the prophets as disciples. Bringing the word of God to the people.

In the first story, we find a certain woman, wife of a man of God, a believer in the Lord. Her husband's death, leaving them in debt. Her and her sons, about to be sold into bondage to pay it.

Elisha asks what does she have, and she replies only a little oil. He tells her to go out to her neighbors and ask for empty containers, and not a few. As many as she can get, and fill them from the pot. And she does as he says, acting on her faith. She fills every vessel they have, and yet there was still more in the pot. She tells Elisha, who says go and sell them and pay her debt, and her and her sons live off what's left over.

In scripture, oil is almost always a picture of the holy Spirit. Debt and bondage, sin and the wages of sin, which is death.

Her husband feared the Lord. He left her with nothing but oil. The Spirit. And she takes that oil and fills the vessels of her neighbors and more. Just as we who are saved are filled with the Spirit, and we can fill others, as vessels, infinitely. It never runs out. The Spirit is enough to not only pay for our debt but to live on, forever.

As men, we should do well to leave our wives and children that inheritance. Greater than any other, the surety of the Spirit in our house, by faith in Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: Living waters flowing out from Jerusalem
teachings.summary: The river from Ezekiel's temple pictures the Spirit and the gospel flowing out from Jerusalem, with believers as fruitful trees by the river as in Psalm 1 and John 7.
teachings.text:
Here in the penultimate chapter of Ezekiel, continuing with the prophecy of the Temple, we find the prophet brought out with the man guiding him before, who had the measure in his hands, and observing the flowing of water out of the altar and beyond the Temple and the courtyard.

And the further they went, the deeper the water became, from his ankle to his knees, to his loins. Eventually, to a mighty river that could not be passed over, deep enough to swim in.

Returning to the river's brink, the shore along a steep rise, and there he observed the trees on both sides. The angels tells him that the waters themselves that issue out of the Temple will eventually fill the desert, and the seas, healing all they touch, everything *shall live whither the river cometh*.

Living waters emanating from Jerusalem, trees lining their banks.

In **Psalm 1**, the Bible says we who delight in the Lord and His word are like unto trees planted by a river, that brings forth fruit, and the leaves shall not whither.

The prophet Zachariah preaches that in the day of the Lord, among the other things that occur, would be Jesus splitting the mount of Olives in Jerusalem, and in that day *living waters* shall go out from Jerusalem.

In the gospel of John, Jesus says that out of the belly of believers shall flow rivers of living water, and that this was a picture of the Spirit which they that believe on Him should receive.

Later, in the Revelation of Jesus given John, the new Heaven and heavenly Jerusalem has a river, and the tree of life upon it, which gives 12 different fruits every month, and whose leaves were for healing the nations.

The natural application for the initial prophecy given Ezekiel is a restored kingdom, with a river of waters healing the land, trees grown up from its shores, and full of all types of fish in abundance.

But spiritually, this is fulfilled in the ministry of Christ, and the spreading of the Gospel, as living waters, the Spirit, and wherever it went, healing the nations, and believers being as trees bearing fruit, other believers, springing up alongside the brink.

Prophetically, this matches the pattern in the end times shown John, of New Jerusalem.

If you are like the righteous man in **Psalm 1**, the believer in **John 7**, you are a tree bearing fruit, and from you flows the Spirit, living waters, His word.

Notice, the river begins in Jerusalem and gets deeper and deeper the further it travels.

And note too, that there are miry places, salt marshes that shall not be healed.

That the Mt Olive prophecy in Zachariah talks about the split, and a war between Judah.

There are those who will not receive the truth. There were Jews who would not believe, and they killed Christ and persecuted His followers.

teachings.title: Not by might, but by my Spirit
teachings.summary: Zechariah's golden candlestick fed by two olive trees shows that the temple is restored by God's Spirit, with lamp oil picturing the Holy Ghost, the olive trees the two witnesses of Revelation, and the candlesticks the churches.
teachings.text:
We are in **Zechariah 4** and the prophet is visited by an angel and a vision, as out of a deep sleep. He sees a golden candle stick with 7 candles, fed by oil from a bowl, with pipes from 2 olive trees beside it. Confused the prophet asks what it is he is being shown.

This is pictured in the instructions for the Tabernacle;

**Exodus 25:31-37**
*And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same. And six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side: Three bowls made like unto almonds, with a knop and a flower in one branch; and three bowls made like almonds in the other branch, with a knop and a flower: so in the six branches that come out of the candlestick. And in the candlesticks shall be four bowls made like unto almonds, with their knops and their flowers. And there shall be a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, according to the six branches that proceed out of the candlestick. Their knops and their branches shall be of the same: all it shall be one beaten work of pure gold. And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof: and they shall light the lamps thereof, that they may give light over against it.*

**Exodus 27:20-21**
*And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always. In the tabernacle of the congregation without the vail, which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the Lord: it shall be a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.*

In the Bible, such as the Parable of the Ten Virgins (**Matthew 25**), lamp oil is a symbol of the Holy Spirit and spiritual preparedness. Here it is the same, the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, that it is by God's Spirit he shall restore the temple and Jerusalem.

The candles are described as being fed continuously by the two olive trees, so filled with oil they pipe it out to fill the bowls directly from their branches. Without a press and refinement. Pure.

In Revelation we learn that the two olive trees that are before the Lord, are the two witnesses. Two great men of God who give prophecy, by the word of God.

There are theories as to who these two men are. Many say Moses and Elijah, those who stood glorified with Christ on the mount of transfiguration. Others believe Elijah and Enoch, both taken up into Heaven, translated without death.

But it would make sense that either way, the continuous light of God's word, fed with the oil of His Spirit, would be upon the rebuilding of the Temple. Where Zerubbabel had laid a foundation but hadn't completed it yet.

The candles themselves represent the Spirit of God upon churches. Upon the house of God.

**Revelation 1:18-20**
*I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death. Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter; The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.*

The 7 candles are also tied to the 7 Spirits of the Lord;

**Revelation 1:4**
*John to the seven churches which are in Asia: Grace be unto you, and peace, from him which is, and which was, and which is to come; and from the seven Spirits which are before his throne;*

**Isaiah 11:2**
*And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord*

teachings.title: The Lord, merciful and gracious, and Jealous
teachings.summary: In Exodus 34 God reveals Himself as merciful yet not clearing the guilty and as Jealous, guarding His people, while the feasts all picture Christ.
teachings.text:
*Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost. And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent.*

Exodus chapter 34 finds Moses in need to hew the rocks into tablets to replace those he broke in his anger at the golden calf and the sin of the children of Israel. The first God hewn, now must be made by Moses that God could give to him the covenant as a record, written in stone.

Only Moses was allowed on Saini, not even the beasts of the field were allowed to graze the foothills nearby.

The Lord came in a cloud and the figure of Christ Jesus (IMO) appeared before him, as the glory of the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed "*The Lord, The Lord God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.*

This is who God is. We who are saved seek to know Him and throughout scripture we are given many names and descriptions that allow us to understand the holy God. Here is the quality of God that is judgment. He is merciful and longsuffering. He forgives. But He does not clear the guilty, and he visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third or fourth generation.

That is not to say they are punished for the sins of the father, but rather their inequities being judgment upon their people for generations. God is about to declare a genocide of the people in the way towards the promised land. The wickedness they have done in His sight. The groves and high places, molten gods and altars. God tells Moses that they are to destroy these people that their wickedness doesn't infect the children of Israel, through practice, through marriage, or in any way including eating meat sacrificed to idols.

We learn a name for God and it is Jealous. He is a jealous God. Jealousy is not envy or covetousness. It is fiercely protecting that which one owns. God is saying in this covenant He owns them, they are His people. And if they go whoring after strange gods because they were snared by covenant to make peace with the people He has judged be destroyed, He will have vengeance upon the children of Israel.

To further defend what is His from whoredoms, going after strange gods, the Lord further emphasizes the ordinances for feasts He has put in place as a memorial for what He has done for the people of Israel, and as a picture of the Messiah to come, Christ Jesus.

The feast of unleavened bread that begins immediately after Passover, which is the sabbaths of Christ when He is 3 days and 3 nights in Hell for our sins. And because His only begotten Son is a sacrifice for us, and because the firstborn sons of the children of Israel were spared in passover, even if their cattle, they belong to God and must be attoned through a substitutionary sacrifice. All a picture of Christ.

The sabbath, again a picture of Christ.

The feast of weeks, which leads to the Pentecost. The firstfruits of the harvest.

Then the feast of the harvest at years end.

All a picture of the time to come, and a memorial for the children of Israel that they may know Jesus.

*Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven; neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left unto the morning.*

The unleavened bread and unfermented wine of the Lord's supper. Taking Jesus down from the cross before sunset on Passover.

The first of the firstfruits are God's under this Mosaic law. All a picture of Christ.

teachings.title: Learn not the way of the heathen
teachings.summary: Astrology and idols are vanity and foolishness before the Creator, and the heathen worship created things rather than the living God.
teachings.text:
We are there in **Jeremiah** chapter 10, and the Lord, speaking through the prophet by the Spirit is casting judgments upon Judah, the remaining children of Israel, this time focusing on their adopting the heathen practices of idol worshiping of graven images. Wood carvings plated with molten metals, hammered into place and carried about for feasts and religious practices.

He begins by warning them not to be caught up in the signs of the sky. Astrology and the movement of the lights in the firmament, given as we read in Genesis as a way to mark time, but being used by those who worship idols and small gods that are of their own wicked imagination. To scare people into thinking catastrophe was nigh.

Babylonians especially had very advanced system of astrological prophesying, and God says this is vanity. Just as the workman and the founder, cutting down trees to make idols to Baal or the Queen of Heaven are vain.

It is important to see things as God sees them. And as He is the creator of all things, His view of the superstitious nonsense men invents to explain His creation, including to worship the things He created, is both insulting to a jealous God, and laughably foolish.

**Romans 1:21-25**
*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

We worship the living God, through Whom all things were made. The heathen in their fear worship the sun, the moon, the stars. Idols made of wood and stone and molten metals.

**Psalm 115:5-8**
*They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not: They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not: They have hands, but they handle not: feet have they, but they walk not: neither speak they through their throat. They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them.*

teachings.title: The Lord is the true and living God
teachings.summary: The idols men make cannot save, but the Lord is the true, living and everlasting King whose wrath cleanses the land of them.
teachings.text:
**Acts 17:22-31**
*Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, To The Unknown God. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Neither is worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation; That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring. Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man's device. And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.*

The Lord is consistently pointing out the vanity, the utter uselessness of these false gods. How foolish it is to bow and serve dead things as gods, that cannot save anyone. They are an invention of man's own vain imagination.

And yet the children of Judah, even those going to Temple and continuing the Levitical ceremonial ordinances and laws, had allowed this idolatry in to their cities. They baked cakes to the "queen of heaven." They participated in feasts to these false gods. They were made to fear the heavens God created, rather than the God who created them.

*But they are altogether brutish and foolish: the stock is a doctrine of vanities.*

And for this cause God is bringing destruction upon Judah, and the graven images and idols decked with golden plates will be destroyed, along with the carvers and founders who made them;

*But the Lord is the true God, he is the living God, and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his indignation. Thus shall ye say unto them, The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens.*
...
*Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them. They are vanity, and the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish*.

The next verse is a prophetic statement of the coming Christ; that despite the people being cast out of the land, and the cities spoiled, there is a portion of Jacob to come;

*The portion of Jacob is not like them: for he is the former of all things; and Israel is the rod of his inheritance: The Lord of hosts is his name.*

God's wrath is cleansing. Making strait the path that leads to His righteousness.

teachings.title: I am the LORD, there is none else
teachings.summary: God's specific prophecy of Cyrus proves He alone is God and that His promise of salvation in Christ is just as sure, and the Israel that shall be saved is all who are Abraham's seed by faith in Christ.
teachings.text:
Continuing the very clear, undeniable, easy to understand prophecy of God through Isaiah, of the future King of the Medo-Persian empire, more than a century off in the future. **Isaiah 45** is one of the most powerful chapters in the Bible.

God says He has named Cyrus as deliverer, for after the Babylonian captivity, still decades away, after the 70 years of desolation in Jerusalem as prophesied, the Babylonian empire will be over thrown, and Cyrus will free the Jews wot return, to rebuild the temple. That the line of David continued to Christ and the place God put His name would stand until it served its purpose, the death burial and resurrection of Jesus.

And just as sure and specific and certain as this prophecy is for Cyrus, so it is for the Messiah.

By this we may know there is no other God beside Him. He is the Lord, and there is none else.

For all creation testifies, and all the prophets gave witness, and all the promises made to the faithful, and the evidence all around that those who trust in Him are never ashamed.

God calls all His shots beforehand, and we see the results are true. And if these things are sure and true, then know the promise of salvation and eternal life in Christ Jesus is as well.

*Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together; I the Lord have created it.*

The Lord has created all things that, in His time, in the end, salvation and righteousness are as a flood upon the earth. And like the flood of Noah, we shall be delivered and those that reject God will be destroyed.

Those that chase after gods of their own hands, who worship the created more than the Creator, shall be confounded and ashamed when the day comes.

*But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.*

The Lord openly declares these things, all that is right. His perfect law. His kept promises. His holy Name.

*I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.*

**John 5:37**
*And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.*

**Philippians 2:9-11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father*

**1 John 5:7**
*For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.*

The word of God is true, let every man be a liar who rejects it. All that are incensed against Him shall be ashamed. Those who do not wish to retain God in their knowledge, who hold the truth in unrighteousness, they will be made to know He loves us.

And in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and glory.

**Galatians 3:27-29**
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

**Romans 11:26-27**
*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Amen

teachings.title: The lot is cast, the disposing is of the Lord
teachings.summary: God gives the heart its words by the Spirit and disposes even the casting of lots, as in Israel's use of lots and the Urim and Thummim, showing His sovereignty and our acceptance of His will.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 16** can be divided into thematic sections, the first of which is dealing with the relationship between the Lord and man, and His work and judgment.

The second, the understanding of kings and man. Third, against pride and for meek wisdom. Fourth, the ungodly, froward, violent and naughty men vs the righteous.

Like chapter 15, **Proverbs 16** is also bookended by similar passages. Here, on the power of God to determine outcomes.

*The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the Lord.*

As Jesus says;

**Mark 13:11**
*But when they shall lead you, and deliver you up, take no thought beforehand what ye shall speak, neither do ye premeditate: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye: for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Ghost.*

If from the abundance of the heart man speaketh, the heart inclined to the Lord will give us the words that are spoken.

*The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord.*

Just as what to say is influenced by the Spirit, the lots of chance are cast to the Lord.

Throughout the Old Testament, lots - or marked sticks, bones or stones, similar to dice in purpose but not design - were used to determine divine will for priestly duties, such as assigning temple service, burning incense, and wood offerings, as described in **1 Chronicles 24:3-5, 19, Luke 1:9**, and **Nehemiah 10:34**. They were used to divide the promised land (**Joshua 14:2, Numbers 26:55**).

The Levitical ordinances required holy lots, called the Urim and the Thummim, as part of the ephod, or official vestiture. The right to use these items was strictly reserved for the Levitical High Priest (**Deuteronomy 33:8**). They functioned similarly to lots, often providing a "yes" or "no" answer to a specific inquiry. For example, in **1 Samuel 14:41,** King Saul asks for the "Thummim" to determine if guilt lay with him or the people.

Ultimately, it left matters to seeming chance, but God's will was the end of the matter once the lots were cast.

The sovereignty of God is found in such things, as giving us the words to speak from His wisdom, or settling a matter by accepting God's will, when the choice isn't clear. Not in micromanaging every outcome, but giving us the heart to understand and the serenity to accept what comes.

teachings.title: Who is a rock save our God
teachings.summary: Psalm 18 shows who the Lord is, our rock and deliverer, and there is no other rock nor name but Jesus, who rewards those who trust Him and destroys the wicked.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 18** is one of the first long-form songs of David, and it reflects his own experience with the Lord, his trust in God, and deliverance from his enemies, while weaving together prophetic views of Jesus, the doctrines of salvation, the end times wrath and Kingdom of God.

Ultimately, the Psalm gives us understanding of Who the Lord is and why He is worthy of our trust, today.

The Lord is our strength. Our rock. Our fortress. Our deliverer. Our strength. Trustworthy. Our buckler, the horn of our salvation, our high tower. He is worthy to be praised. He is merciful to those that are merciful. Upright in all His ways to those that walk in them. Pure to the pure and froward to the froward.

His way is perfect, His word is tried and trusted, and the strength and shield of those that place that trust in Him.

*For who is God save the LORD? or who is a rock save our God?*

There is no other rock than the Lord. There is no other name given but Jesus. He is the fulfillment of the word, the word made flesh, the promise of God come down from Heaven. The Christ. And He liveth.

The shield of salvation is given, by the right-hand of God. His gentleness has made those who trust Him great.

*The LORD liveth; and blessed be my rock; and let the God of my salvation be exalted.*

The Lord is praised among the heathen. The strangers hear and obey. The people who were not a people are come, and are subdued under the throne of David, to his Seed. To His anointed, evermore.

The enemies of David, like the enemies of Christ, are crushed before them by the fiery and fierce judgment of God. Rains of fire and brimstone, hail and lightenings, leading the wicked to cry out, and hide themselves from His fury. And ultimately be destroyed by His coming.

The Lord then is a rewarder of those that trust in Him, who diligently seek Him. Who follow His ways and obey His statutes. He will reward us for the righteousness we have shown, and the recompense for our cleanliness in His sight. The righteousness of Christ imputed on His children. The gold, silver and precious stones we build upon that foundation.

He lifts us up, strengthening us to do great deeds in His name. He fills us with His light.

He hears our cries. He comes to our aid. He destroys the wicked for our sake, in the anger kindled by their sin against Him and their treatment of His children.

*Therefore will I give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen, and sing praises unto thy name.* Amen

teachings.title: I am the resurrection and the life
teachings.summary: Jesus wept as one touched with our infirmities, and His word to Martha that whoever believes in Him shall never die is salvation by faith and eternal security.
teachings.text:
Jesus wept. The shortest verse in the Bible and perhaps one of the most powerful.
