Here his friend Lazarus has died, and his sisters are mourning and the emotion overwhelms Jesus even knowing He can and will raise Lazarus up. The pain of life and grief is something that Jesus being fully man experienced and understands.

“*For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin*.” **Hebrew 4:15**

And so, Jesus wept. And then raised Lazarus from the dead.

It's one of the most beautiful stories of His ministry on earth, and as Martha testifies her faith that her brother shared, that he shall rise again in the resurrection of the last day. Jesus expounds on this with the full Gospel, yet again:

*I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.*

Martha confesses the truth of the Gospel Jesus gives, the truth her brother and sister also believe. That those who believe on Him shall never die, but he shall live. This is salvation by faith and eternal security, yet again. 11 chapters in and in every one so far, this is the good news as given by Christ.

If you doubt His word is true, I don't know what else one could say to bring you to believe.

teachings.title: Christ the physician of sinners
teachings.summary: Christ forgiving the palsied man's sins proves His deity, and His call to sinners shows all need the physician, made clean by His imputed righteousness, not by their own.
teachings.text:
The healing of the man lowered by 4 into a full house where Jesus was preaching is a beautiful picture how many with faith may bring us to salvation. Jesus forgiving his sins, and then healing his flesh in opposition to the scribes questioning in their hearts His authority gives a definitive statement of the divinity of Christ. "Who can forgive sins but God only?" Exactly.

Notice it's the faith expressed, not only of the man with palsy, but those who bring him to Jesus that moves Christ. It is the faith that leads to His forgiveness of sin. The healing of infirmity comes after. This is such a picture of salvation and the moving of the Spirit in a saved Christian's life. And notice, all to the glory of God. "*They were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.*"

Next we see Jesus call upon a publican, a tax collector, identified here and in Luke as Levi, but better known as the Apostle Matthew. Jesus calls him from his position collecting tax on the goods coming into port in Capernaum and bids the publican to follow Him and he does.

A Levite publican, a double blow to the worldly Pharisees. One of their own collecting tribute for Rome. No greater sinner in their mind, and to dine with one, that would be "unclean."

Jesus's answer to their outrage, that He was here as a physician, to heal the sick, calling the sinners to repentance towards God, as the righteous have no need of a "doctor," is a backhanded insult to the Pharisees. They are not righteous. There is none righteous by the works of the law, and certainly not these hypocrites. But their own conceit would keep them from seeing His point. In matters of righteousness we are all in need of a physician, Christ Jesus.

We shouldn't lose sight of that truth, and understand it's not the sins that make us clean or unclean.

It's not our own righteousness in following the law, but our hearts and spirit of faith in Christ Jesus to impute His righteousness on us that heals. That makes us clean. Washed in the blood.

There is a natural man argument that many unsaved scoffers and reprobates make is that Jesus "hung out with the sinners" and not the "holy rollers." They take this verse and blaspheme, claiming Jesus liked to "party with sinners" to excuse their own unregenerate lifestyle.

Of course they meltdown when you correct them that He certainly preached to the sinners to bring them out of sin, but actually hung out with, was friends with, His Apostles and closest disciples.

That physicians don't "hang out" with the sick, they treat them to be well. This understanding escapes them, and I have seen more than a few Christians unable to make this distinction and get confused or browbeaten into not calling out sin. Ignoring the sickness. Enabling the worst behaviors, simply to not be seen as a "Pharisee."

Both the hypocritical fruit inspectors and degenerates are sick and in need of a physician.

teachings.title: Son of David and Son of God
teachings.summary: Luke's genealogy places Jesus in David's line as the promised King while He is also the Son of God, the two sonships of one who is fully God and fully man.
teachings.text:
Luke, having established the time and circumstances surrounding these events, then gives his version of the generations of Jesus, going from his stepfather Joseph's lineage. Perfect in his generations, all the way back to Adam, who we are reminded, was begat of God.

Being the son of Joseph, even adopted, places Jesus in line for the throne of David, fulfilling the prophets sayings that there will be a King from the root of Jesse, a descendant of David, who would rule and reign forever. The Son of David.

To the more secular, this places Jesus in line to be an earthly king. To make the Christ the physical deliverer of Israel. But to those called by the Spirit, and given understanding of scripture, the savior of their souls and heir to the Heavenly Kingdom. The Son of God.

It is these two sonships that Jesus was born into. Fully God. Fully man. And the conflict in the hearts of those who hear of Him, even those who directly saw Him walk among them performing miracles and preaching on the Kingdom of God, would set the stage for His ministry.

teachings.title: Created for His pleasure
teachings.summary: As Christ, equal with God, submitted to the Father and was exalted, we must submit to God's will and to earthly order for His pleasure.
teachings.text:
The glory and Majesty of the Lord God, by Whom all things were made for His pleasure, and before whom we are not worthy. Who in His magnificent power and wisdom, is perfect and holy.

And it is this same God, to whom only the hinder parts could be seen by mortal eyes, Who when He passed Moses could not bear to witness, and the flow of Moses face from being in His presence made the children of Israel turn away in shame. God who is worthy of praise and service. Serving with fear and trembling at His perfect will set before us in His word. So much so, our submission unto earthly hierarchy is done in submission to Him that set all things in the heavens and upon the earth, to please Him.

As Christ, who thought it not blasphemy to declare Himself equal to God, submitted Himself to the will of the Father. So we must submit ourselves to doing what we are created for; giving pleasure to God.

For Jesus is the equal of God, but submitted unto God, and there by was given glory and is exalted above everything:

**Philippians 2:6-11**
Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

**John 6:38-40**
 *For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

teachings.title: The earnest of our inheritance
teachings.summary: The Holy Spirit is God's earnest, sealing believers as His purchased possession until the redemption of the body.
teachings.text:
*O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.*

**Romans 7** explains the war within the saved between the spirit and the flesh, that the flesh worketh the law of sin, while the Spirit worketh the law of God. That our flesh has us do what we would not. And not do what we would. That our temporal bodies are in a battle with the new man, the quickened spirit within us, the Spirit of God that resides in our hearts.

But that if we walk after the Spirit, we will do the things of God. But if we walk after the flesh, we will go after the lusts of the flesh.

But we are delivered from this mortal body. The promise of God is that as we receive the Spirit as the earnest of our adoption, that the day of redemption is when it is fulfilled with a glorified body, unto eternal life and without the temptations of the flesh.

**Ephesians 1:12-14**
*That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ. In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

Earnest is money, sometimes called a “good faith deposit,” is a sum that is included with your offer to purchase something to show your seriousness of intent to go through with the purchase, which is also called redemption. The Spirit is the earnest of God, given in Christ, sealing us as His until the resurrection, whereby we are redeemed.

**1 Corinthians 6:20**
*For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.*

teachings.title: Wisdom from everlasting is the Word
teachings.summary: Wisdom in Proverbs 8, crying out to all and with God from everlasting before creation, is the Word, Jesus Christ, the way, the truth and the life.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 8 (& 9)**, are an Ode to Wisdom, the Word and Spirit of God, with Him in the beginning , through Whom all creation was made.

Wisdom cries out from all creation, from the top of the mountains, in the high places and in the paths. The Lord's way is wisdom. In the coming and going of the city. At its gates and doors.

Like God calls to all men, as Jesus lifted up, wisdom calls out to all. To the simple and fools. To those who love wisdom and seek her excellent things, her right things. To those that seek truth.

**John 14:6** *Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.*

**Matthew 7:7** *Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you*

**John 8:32** *And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free*

The words of wisdom are the word of God, and there is nothing perverse or froward in them. Holy and plain to those that listen.

More precious than any treasures, wisdom is better than gold. With wisdom dwells prudence; Wisdom applied to practice. Discernment and action according to knowledge.

The wise hate evil; pride and arrogance, froward mouths they hate.

By wisdom kings and princes rule.

*I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me*.

The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.

**Psalm 63:1** *O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is*

The Lord's wisdom is from everlasting, His word. Before all creation, He is. Eternally with Him, as one brought up together.

**John 1:1-2** *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God.*

Blessed is the man who finds wisdom. They receive life and favor of the Lord. They live in His grace.

But woe to those that hate wisdom. *All they that hate me love death.*

teachings.title: Gather my saints together unto me
teachings.summary: Psalm 50, a prophecy of Asaph the seer in God's own voice, shows Christ the Creator returning in fire to judge, and the gathering of His saints before His wrath is poured out, proving the rapture is no new doctrine.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 50**, is a song written directly from the voice of God to His people, His own perspective directly to man. It is instruction in doctrine and prophecy, by His word. In the first person.

He spoke these things through a psalmist other than David. The superscript titles this as "A Psalm of Asaph," making it the very first of the 12 "Asaphite Psalms" in the Bible.

Asaph was a prominent Levite, appointed by King David as the chief musician and worship leader before the Ark of the Covenant when it was brought to Jerusalem. More than just a song director, the Bible credits him as a prophet. A seer.

**2 Chronicles 29:30**
*Moreover Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the LORD with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped.*

While prophesying may refer to preaching the word of God, seer is the specific term for a visionary who is given glimpses of the future by God, prophetic understanding of things that are not but will be.

He begins his song by introducing its Author. The mighty God. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, it is God breathed, and spoken. But this will be the word of God, as a message of judgment for His people.

It establishes first the primacy of God, the Creator. By His Word the earth and the heavens were made.

**John 1:1–4**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men.*

It is important when we see credit for creation to God in the Bible, to remember that this includes Jesus.

**1 Corinthians 8:6**
*But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.*

We have a New Testament understanding when we reflect on the Old Testament revelations. The nature of the Godhead is revealed in the creation. And it is relevant to this Psalm.

Out of Zion, the place God chose to put His name, God hath shined.

His presence in the Tabernacle and the eventual Temple, God with His people through their worship, is an echo to the true coming of the Lord in the flesh, and His return on His day to judge the nations, upon that holy mountain.

*Our God shall come, and shall not keep silence: a fire shall devour before him, and it shall be very tempestuous round about him.*

The Second Coming, the return of Christ, is the day we all look forward to with gladness. He will come with power, a consuming fire proceeding from Him, and the sword of His word from His mouth shall slay the wicked.

**2 Thessalonians 1:7–9**
*And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power*

The future judgment of the world was a key part of the Israelites understanding, though through a glass darkly. However, having the full revelation of the complete Bible, we see clearly what they only glimpsed in faith.

He comes as a judge, the Son calling up to Heaven, and down to Earth, with a shout, with trumpet, the call to judgment of His people, before His wrath is poured out on the world.

*Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice. And the heavens shall declare his righteousness: for God is judge himself. Selah.*

The gathering of the elect, those sanctified by the Spirit in Christ, is not a "new doctrine," as some would claim. The Rapture, or the gathering of the elect being caught up together to meet the Lord in the air, was a key part of prophecy for the Lord's people.
